relationships.title: OpenAI letter of intent: up to $100 billion as each gigawatt is deployed
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia's {headline} letter of intent with {counterparty} produced no disclosed definitive agreement; a separate equity purchase followed, so the headline adds no binding exposure.
relationships.definition: In September 2025 Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent under which Nvidia intends to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as each gigawatt of Nvidia systems is deployed, alongside OpenAI deploying at least 10 GW. Both sides said details were still to be finalized. No definitive agreement for this structure has been disclosed by either side as of 2026-11-23; in February 2026 Nvidia instead committed equity to OpenAI's funding round, recorded separately.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia release: intends to invest up to $100 billion progressively (ev_30021). Q3 FY26 10-Q: a letter of intent with an opportunity to invest in OpenAI (ev_10156). FY26 10-K (2026-02-25): finalizing an investment and partnership agreement (ev_10125). Q1 and Q2 FY27 10-Qs do not name OpenAI as an investee.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: OpenAI release of the same date: NVIDIA intends to invest up to $100 billion progressively (ev_120020), details to be finalized (ev_120021). OpenAI has published nothing since that converts the letter of intent into a definitive agreement; its February 2026 round release describes a separate $30B investment.

credit.wwr_reason: No binding exposure. If converted, equity value would fall with AI demand and OpenAI's funding conditions, but the amount would not grow with distress.
credit.notes: Tier 2 reporting (not quotable here) said the letter of intent was stalled in early 2026 and that the February 2026 investment was separate from it. Listed under Needs quote in the R5 report.

first_order.trigger: OpenAI deploys gigawatts of Nvidia systems without a definitive investment agreement
first_order.mechanism: The letter of intent lapses in practice and Nvidia's cash stays uncommitted
first_order.text: If OpenAI keeps deploying Nvidia systems without the letter of intent being signed into a contract, Nvidia gains the sales without the per gigawatt investment.

first_order.trigger: Nvidia and OpenAI sign a definitive agreement on the gigawatt structure
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia would owe equity to OpenAI as each gigawatt is deployed
first_order.text: A signed version would turn the headline into a contingent commitment tied to OpenAI's own Nvidia purchases, which is vendor financing by another name.

second_order.trigger: Market reads the headline as committed money
second_order.mechanism: OpenAI's suppliers and lessors price OpenAI's capacity to pay on a commitment that does not bind Nvidia
second_order.text: Lessors and clouds that counted on Nvidia money reaching OpenAI could find that the headline never funds, weakening the case for OpenAI's leases.

relationships.notes: Kept separate from rel_openai_eq_2026. No source states that the February 2026 investment replaces or counts against the letter of intent; treat the letter of intent as unexecuted as of 2026-11-23. Gate R: status changed from letter of intent to restructured. Nvidia's annual report filed 2026-02-25 says it was finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI (ev_140027); OpenAI's round naming Nvidia followed (rel_openai_eq_2026); Nvidia's two later quarterly reports do not mention the letter of intent. Analysis: no source says the letter of intent was terminated or that the later purchase counts against it.

relationships.title: OpenAI 2026 funding round: Nvidia named for $30B
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia committed {committed_total} to {counterparty}'s {dates.announced:year} round, yet neither company has disclosed how much Nvidia has actually paid in.
relationships.definition: On 2026-02-27 OpenAI announced $110B of new investment at a $730B pre-money valuation, including $30B from NVIDIA, under a Series C Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement dated the same day. OpenAI closed the round on 2026-03-31 with $122 billion of committed capital, anchored by Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank. Nvidia's own filings do not name the investment, its instrument, tranches or the amount paid.

committed_total.note: OpenAI names $30B from NVIDIA in the round it closed on 2026-03-31 with committed capital (ev_120015, ev_120017); Nvidia does not disclose it.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23 that names this investment. The FY26 10-K (filed 2026-02-25) says Nvidia was finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI (ev_10125, recorded on the letter of intent). Later filings refer only to equity commitments in AI model makers or frontier labs, unnamed: $20 billion at 2026-10-25 (ev_120008, ev_120010, ev_120011).
reconciliation.counterparty_side: OpenAI: $30B from NVIDIA in the $110B round at $730B pre-money (ev_120098); round closed with $122 billion committed at $852 billion post-money, anchored by NVIDIA (ev_120015, ev_120016, ev_120017). OpenAI's equity commitment letter with Amazon, filed by Amazon, names NVIDIA Corporation as an investor in the company (ev_120031) and the Series C Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement of 2026-02-27 (ev_120032).

credit.wwr_reason: Equity loss is capped at cost and moves with OpenAI's valuation and the AI demand cycle; the amount does not grow if OpenAI weakens.
credit.collateral: None. Instrument: the round was documented as Series C preferred stock (ev_120032); Nvidia's own security is not stated.
credit.notes: Headline and committed rest on OpenAI's release only (tier 1, counterparty side); Nvidia has not named the deal. Funded is unknown. Payment timing is unknown: SoftBank's parallel $30.0 billion was paid in three $10 billion tranches in April, July and October 2026 (ev_120103, ev_120104), but no source states Nvidia's schedule. Analysis: Nvidia's undisclosed equity commitments fell from $27 billion (April 2026) to $25 billion (July) and $20 billion (October), consistent with but not proof of tranche payments.

first_order.text: A down round at OpenAI would force Nvidia to impair its OpenAI stake through other income, because the measurement alternative uses observable transactions.

relationships.title: Guaranties of OpenAI's PORTS-Pike leases from SB Energy, capped at $105 billion
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia guarantees {counterparty}'s rent at an Ohio campus up to {contingent_max}, so Nvidia must pay exactly when {counterparty} cannot.
relationships.definition: On 2026-08-17 Nvidia entered into residual value guaranties with SB Energy, the lessor, covering about 4.25 GW of IT load leased for 20 years to an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC at the PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio. Nvidia pays only if OpenAI's tenant defaults (insolvency or an uncured monetary default); each guaranty takes effect when its building is ready for service, the first expected in Nvidia's fiscal 2029, and the guaranteed amount declines as OpenAI pays rent. The aggregate cap is $105 billion; the guaranties end on OpenAI reaching a designated credit rating, at lease end, or after 20 years, and OpenAI must reimburse Nvidia. The tenant is VELA I Holdings, LLC, whose parent OpenAI Global, LLC guarantees its obligations by joinder; OpenAI's non-payment is the trigger, so the exposure is recorded against OpenAI, and SB Energy's building subsidiaries are the beneficiaries.

contingent_max.trigger: Insolvency of the OpenAI tenant or an uncured monetary default under a PORTS-Pike lease, after the building is ready for service; Nvidia pays the shortfall against a guaranteed minimum value that declines over each 20-year lease, net of reletting or sale.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: 8-K and 10-Q: guaranties capped at $105 billion for about 4.25 GW, nine phases, first effective in fiscal 2029, triggered by tenant default, exposure declines as OpenAI pays, terminates on a satisfactory OpenAI credit rating, OpenAI reimburses Nvidia, option on about 3.8 GW more (ev_30001, ev_30009, ev_10040, ev_120001, ev_120002, ev_120005, ev_30007, ev_30008, ev_30004). No payments made to date (ev_30023).
reconciliation.counterparty_side: OpenAI: secures about 8 GW-IT; 20-year lease; NVIDIA provides credit support for the initial 4.25 IT-GW; rent starts only as completed capacity is delivered (ev_120022, ev_120025, ev_120024, ev_120023). SB Energy S-1/A: aggregate guaranteed value and remedy cap of $105 billion on the initial 4.25 GW-IT; trigger is tenant insolvency or an uncured monetary default; OpenAI compensates NVIDIA under a separate agreement; 17 leases for about 8.0 GW-IT commencing 2028 to 2032 (ev_40089, ev_40090, ev_40091, ev_40094, ev_40098, ev_40099).

differences.nvidia_value: Site exclusivity for NVIDIA infrastructure given in exchange (10-Q)
differences.counterparty_value: Compensation provided separately by OpenAI under a separate agreement, amount not disclosed (SB Energy)
OpenAI must secure a replacement guarantor rated at least A- (SB Energy)

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia pays only when OpenAI cannot pay rent, so the exposure is drawn exactly as OpenAI's credit fails; SB Energy states OpenAI is not an investment-grade tenant.
credit.collateral: No security for Nvidia. The landlord must pursue the tenant parent concurrently (ev_100050) and Nvidia looks solely to the tenant and tenant parent for recoupment (ev_100003). On a trigger Nvidia may assume the tenancy, have the landlord re-let, or sell (ev_40096); recovery depends on reletting a campus purpose-built for Nvidia infrastructure. OpenAI's reimbursement and indemnity is an unsecured claim on the defaulted tenant (ev_30008, ev_120007).
credit.tenor: Per building up to 20 years from lease commencement; leases commence in stages from 2028 to 2032, so the last guaranty can run into the early 2050s (analysis).
credit.notes: Not effective yet: no building is ready for service; exposure builds building by building and then declines (ev_120009). The guaranties are limited to defined portions of lease and power payments (ev_120003). Nvidia's option on the remaining capacity is at its sole discretion and carries no stated amount.

first_order.trigger: OpenAI's tenant becomes insolvent or misses rent after a PORTS-Pike building is ready
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia pays SB Energy the shortfall up to the declining guaranteed value
first_order.text: If OpenAI stops paying rent at PORTS-Pike, Nvidia owes SB Energy the guaranteed value and holds only an unsecured reimbursement claim on OpenAI.

first_order.trigger: OpenAI reaches the designated credit rating
first_order.mechanism: The guaranties terminate and Nvidia is released
first_order.text: An investment grade rating for OpenAI Group PBC would release Nvidia from the guaranties, so Nvidia's exposure depends directly on OpenAI's credit path.

first_order.trigger: OpenAI weakens while buildings are still being delivered between 2028 and 2032
first_order.mechanism: Each newly ready building adds guaranteed value just as the tenant's credit deteriorates
first_order.text: Because guaranties switch on building by building, a slowdown at OpenAI during construction raises Nvidia's exposure at the worst time.

second_order.trigger: Nvidia's guaranty is withdrawn, not exercised for the option, or doubted
second_order.mechanism: SB Energy's lenders lose the credit support that makes the OpenAI leases financeable
second_order.text: SB Energy says PORTS-Pike's financeability depends on the Nvidia guaranty of OpenAI's lease, so project lenders are underwriting Nvidia's credit, not OpenAI's.

second_order.trigger: OpenAI defaults and Nvidia assumes the tenancy
second_order.mechanism: A campus that exclusively hosts Nvidia infrastructure must be re-let or sold
second_order.text: A default by OpenAI would leave Nvidia seeking a new tenant for gigawatts of Nvidia-only capacity, testing what that capacity is worth without OpenAI.

second_order.mechanism: SB Energy's backlog is mostly PORTS-Pike rent from OpenAI
second_order.text: PORTS-Pike makes up most of SB Energy's backlog, so OpenAI's credit drives SB Energy and its controlling shareholder SoftBank as well as Nvidia.

depth2_links.description: Lessor of PORTS-Pike to the OpenAI affiliate under 17 leases of 20 years (about 8.0 GW-IT, commencing 2028 to 2032) and beneficiary of the Nvidia guaranties on the first 4.25 GW-IT. Its data center backlog of about $430 billion is mostly PORTS-Pike.

amount.note: SB Energy data center segment backlog, all tenants; substantial majority PORTS-Pike

depth2_links.description: Controlling shareholder of SB Energy; OpenAI and NVIDIA are also strategic investors in SB Energy.

relationships.notes: Executed Building 1 guaranty and form: see research/reports/R5_cluster_de.md, Guaranty terms (ev_100001 to ev_100051): tenant VELA I Holdings, LLC (ev_100008), tenant parent OpenAI Global, LLC (ev_100009), letter agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC (ev_100010), guaranteed minimum value constant then declining (ev_100014), no covered project debt in place yet (ev_100020). Coordinate with the vehicle cluster (SB Energy). Nvidia's separate $3.0 billion equity in SB Energy belongs to that cluster. Seniority recorded as guarantor. Dates: signed and filed 2026-08-17; effective left null because no guaranty is in force until the first building is ready for service, expected in fiscal 2029 (ev_120002, ev_30027); maturity left null because it differs per building (up to 20 years from each lease commencement). Tier 2 history: late July 2026 reports of talks on a backstop of up to $250 billion were cut to the signed $105 billion cap (needs quote, see R5 report).

relationships.definition: On 2025-11-18 Nvidia and Microsoft committed to invest up to $10 billion and up to $5 billion in Anthropic, which committed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute and up to 1 GW of compute on Nvidia Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. Nvidia's 10-Q calls it an agreement, subject to closing conditions. Anthropic's February 2026 Series G included a portion of the previously announced Nvidia investment; neither side has disclosed the amount of that portion.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Q3 FY26 10-Q: agreed, subject to certain closing conditions, to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic (ev_10157). Nvidia blog: committing to invest up to $10 billion (ev_30050). Q4 FY26 release: announced an investment (ev_30031). No funded amount disclosed.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: Anthropic: NVIDIA committing to invest up to $10 billion (ev_120062); Series G of 2026-02-12 includes a portion of the previously announced NVIDIA investment (ev_120066). The 424B4 does not list Nvidia among related-person purchasers of Series G-1.

differences.counterparty_value: A portion funded in Series G, amount not disclosed

credit.wwr_reason: Equity value tracks Anthropic and the AI cycle; exposure does not grow if Anthropic weakens.
credit.notes: Committed and funded stay unknown: up to wording, and the Series G portion is not quantified. Whether the $10.0 billion IPO private placement (rel_anthropic_eq_2026) counts against this up to $10 billion is not stated by either side; if it did, the total would exceed the headline, so the two are recorded separately.

first_order.mechanism: Nvidia's preferred stake converted at the IPO is marked down

relationships.title: SpaceX Class A shares held by Nvidia, from its xAI Series E investment
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia holds {counterparty} shares worth {market_value} that began as an xAI investment, in a company that also buys Nvidia systems.
relationships.definition: Nvidia was a strategic investor in xAI's $20 billion Series E, announced 2026-01-06. SpaceX acquired xAI on 2026-02-02, and each xAI preferred share, including Series E, converted into 0.1433 SpaceX Class A shares before a five-for-one split. After SpaceX listed in June 2026, Nvidia's 13F reported 122,764,805 Class A shares at 2026-06-30 and 130,472,925 shares worth $19.68 billion at 2026-09-30.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: 13F-HR: SPACE EXPLORATION TECHN CORP Class A, 122,764,805 shares, $20.98 billion at 2026-06-30 (new position) and 130,472,925 shares, $19.68 billion at 2026-09-30 (ev_50030, ev_50031). Nvidia filings name SpaceXAI and SpaceXSI only as customers (ev_120013, ev_120014); no cost or investment terms.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: xAI release: NVIDIA a strategic investor in the $20B Series E (ev_120096, ev_120097). SpaceX 424B4: xAI acquired 2026-02-02; xAI preferred converted at 0.1433 SpaceX Class A per share pre-split; five-for-one split (ev_120072, ev_120073, ev_120074). SpaceX's 424B4 and 10-Q do not name Nvidia as a holder or state its investment amount.

differences.counterparty_value: No SpaceX disclosure explains an issuance to Nvidia; SpaceX issued shares in the Cursor merger on 2026-08-14, but no allowed source names Nvidia as a Cursor holder

credit.wwr_reason: Listed equity; value falls with SpaceX's AI segment and the AI cycle, capped at cost; no contingent exposure.
credit.notes: Cost basis unknown. Analysis only: at the Tesla Series E conversion (USD 2,000 million into 3.8 million pre-split shares, ev_120080), Nvidia's 122.8 million post-split shares would imply a much larger xAI investment than any figure quotable here; the path from Series E to the 13F count is not fully established. A single anonymous tier 2 report puts Nvidia's xAI investment at $10 billion (needs quote). Market value from the 13F is tier 1 as of 2026-09-30 only.

first_order.trigger: SpaceX shares fall on AI segment losses
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia's mark-to-market on a listed holding drops
first_order.text: SpaceX's AI segment carries heavy GPU spending, so weaker returns at SpaceXSI lower the value of Nvidia's SpaceX shares through other income.

first_order.trigger: SpaceX buys Nvidia GPUs with Valor and Apollo lease financing
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia sells systems to a company in which it holds stock
first_order.text: SpaceX finances Nvidia GPUs through Valor leases and a planned Apollo finance lease, so Nvidia's stake sits next to sales that depend on SpaceX's leasing capacity.

second_order.trigger: Anthropic cancels SpaceXAI capacity after the initial periods
second_order.mechanism: SpaceX loses its largest disclosed AI compute customer while lease payments to Valor continue
second_order.text: Anthropic can cancel SpaceXAI capacity on ninety days notice from early 2027, while SpaceX keeps paying Valor for the GPUs it leased.

second_order.trigger: GPU values fall before the Valor and Apollo leases run off
second_order.mechanism: Lessors hold GPU collateral whose value depends on Nvidia's product cycle
second_order.text: Valor and the Apollo-managed lessor own GPUs leased to SpaceX, so a faster Nvidia product cycle cuts the collateral behind SpaceX's AI leases.

depth2_links.description: Valor leases computing equipment to xAI subsidiaries under three leases with aggregate payments of about $20.2 billion, guaranteed by SpaceX; recorded as failed sale-leaseback debt of $12.9 billion at 2026-09-30.
Apollo-managed lessor: binding commitment letter of 2026-10-24 for a GPU master finance lease, about $40 billion of principal, schedules from the first half of 2027, subject to closing.
Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 for about 325,000 NVIDIA GPUs at Colossus (424B4); later expanded to up to $120.5 billion.
Tesla agreed in January 2026 to invest USD 2,000 million in xAI Series E, settled in SpaceX Class A shares after the merger.

relationships.notes: Seed A3 (Nvidia up to $2 billion in an SPV that buys GPUs leased to xAI) is not confirmed: SpaceX discloses the Valor equipment leases but no allowed source quotable here places Nvidia money in the lessor. Recorded as context in depth2_links only.

events.summary: Nvidia and OpenAI sign a letter of intent: Nvidia intends to invest up to $100 billion as each gigawatt is deployed.
Nvidia's Q3 FY26 10-Q describes a letter of intent with an opportunity to invest in OpenAI.
Nvidia's FY26 10-K says it is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI.
OpenAI announces new investment including $30B from Nvidia under a Series C purchase agreement dated the same day.
OpenAI closes the round with $122 billion of committed capital, anchored by Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank.
Nvidia signs residual value guaranties with SB Energy for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike leases, capped at $105 billion.
Nvidia reports maximum exposure of $105.0 billion to the SB Energy guarantees and no payments to date.
SB Energy's S-1/A describes the guaranty trigger, remedy cap and OpenAI's non-investment grade status.
Nvidia and Microsoft commit to invest up to $10 billion and up to $5 billion in Anthropic.
Nvidia's 10-Q states it agreed, subject to closing conditions, to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic.
Anthropic's Series G includes a portion of Nvidia's previously announced investment; amount not disclosed.
Anthropic's final prospectus: Nvidia to buy 120,481,927 Class N shares for about $10.0 billion at the IPO price.
Anthropic closes the IPO and the $26.0 billion concurrent private placement including Nvidia.
xAI closes its $20B Series E with Nvidia as a strategic investor.
SpaceX acquires xAI; xAI preferred stock converts into SpaceX Class A common stock.
Nvidia's 13F shows a new position of 122,764,805 SpaceX Class A shares at 2026-06-30.
Nvidia's 13F shows 130,472,925 SpaceX Class A shares worth $19.68 billion at 2026-09-30.
Nvidia's annual report says it is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI, in place of the letter of intent wording.
